name: Bolívar
summary_text: The murder of Nawar Jiménez, a trans social leader who campaigned with the "No Es Hora De Callar" movement and joined its sixth symbolic return march of 500+ survivors of sexual violence, is documented in Bolívar on 22 May 2025; she was killed in Carmen de Bolívar, and more than 19 days after the killing the circumstances of what happened remain unclear (friend and fellow leader Yirley Velasco recalls her as a trans-rights fighter in the municipality). El Tiempo's data-journalism work on the gap between official Fiscalía and NGO (Caribe Afirmativo/Defensoría) figures names her case specifically. Bolívar appears within the Caribbean-coast cluster flagged by Caribe Afirmativo's 2025 territorial-expansion finding, where state response is weakest. Versus the national score (~0.52), Bolívar sits approximately 0.08 lower: the killing is a named, targeted murder of a community leader (not an undifferentiated count), and the department falls within the "territorial expansion" zone where the monitoring body documents insufficient state protection. Versus Antioquia (0.33), Bolívar is substantially higher because it carries one specific high-profile homicide rather than the 45-of-270 structural concentration and multi-case impunity pattern defining Antioquia. Versus Atlántico (0.43), Bolívar is marginally above: its evidence is a single named killing within an aggregate warning, whereas Atlántico carries a forward-looking escalation call-out tied to a larger trans sex-work hub.

sources.title: Crímenes Lgbtiq+: las contradictorias cifras entre el Estado y las organizaciones sociales
sources.claim_summary: National daily data-journalism piece (15 June 2025) on contradictory LGBTIQ+ crime figures between the state and social organisations: documents the trans-feminicide of social leader Nawar Jiménez in Bolívar (Carmen de Bolívar) on 22 May 2025 - she had campaigned with the No Es Hora De Callar movement and joined its sixth symbolic return march with 500+ women survivors of sexual violence; her friend and fellow leader Yirley Velasco remembers her; more than 19 days after the killing the circumstances remained unclear.

sources.title: Colombia enfrenta una crisis estructural de violencia contra personas LGBTIQ+: una persona fue asesinada cada 32 horas en 2025 – Corporación Caribe Afirmativo
sources.claim_summary: Caribe Afirmativo 2025 report: one LGBTIQ+ person killed every 32 hours nationally (270 total); violence concentrated in major urban centres but expanding into territories with armed actors and illegal economies - the Caribbean-coast departments including Bolívar sit inside this expansion zone with insufficient documented state protection; threats act as territorial-control mechanisms (1,184 in 2025).
